items.body:

Before opening the issue, please check that there isn't another issue addressing the same problem already created -->

## Module
sale_stock_picking_invoice_link and purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link

## Describe the bug
these modules use location type (customer and vendor) to calculate pickings but there are cases where other location types are being used:

1) subcontracting: Subcontracting Location type is 'internal'. who can we include this? 
2) inter company transfers: Inter-company transit location type is 'transit' which can easily be included.


## To Reproduce
**Affected versions**:

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. create a subcontracting or inter company sales purchase
2. it will not link them to corresponding sales/purchase

**Expected behavior**
It would be good to handle these cases.

items.title: [20.0][MIG] sale_stock_picking_invoice_link: Migration to 20.0
items.body:
Migration of `sale_stock_picking_invoice_link` to 20.0.

### What the jump needed

- **`uom.uom.rounding` is gone** ([9a4ad7cc18d3](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/commit/9a4ad7cc18d3), `[REF] *: remove 'uom.uom.rounding' field`). The check on the quantity left to invoice now calls `uom.is_zero()`, which rounds with the same `Product Unit` decimal precision the removed field exposed.
- **The return wizard `stock.return.picking` is gone** ([36b4a0f5fb2b](https://github.com/odoo/odoo/commit/36b4a0f5fb2b), `[REM] stock: remove return wizard`). Two tests used it to build the return; they now call `stock.picking._create_return()`. The return move inherits `to_refund` from the original move and its demand starts at 0, so the test sets `product_uom_qty`.
- **ruff**: the 20.0 branch pins 0.16.8 and 19.0 pins 0.13.0, so `PERF102` now fails on `setUpClass`, in code this migration does not otherwise touch. `company_data` is a plain dict and the key was unused.

### It also carries the fix of #2535

#2535 (`[FIX] ... link deliveries to the invoice, not the refund`) is still open against 19.0. Without it the bug travels to 20.0: `stock_account` sets `to_refund` by `default=True` on every move, so an outgoing move of an order that has a credit note gets linked to the credit note and the invoice ends up with no pickings. If you want this PR to be the migration only, I can drop that commit and port the fix separately once #2535 is merged.

One note on it: **the `sudo()` it adds on the write is not needed in 20.0**. In 20.0 `stock_account` runs `_action_done` as superuser (`self = self.sudo()`, `stock_account/models/stock_move.py:249`), which 19.0 does not do (`:177`), so the write already runs with `sudo()` when a delivery is validated. It is kept to stay identical to the 19.0 fix. On 20.0 its test asserts the symptom instead: the invoice shows its delivery and the credit note does not.

### Migration script

`migrations/20.0.1.0.0/post-migration.py` re-links the deliveries that the old behaviour wrote against the credit note: the code fix only covers what is written from now on, so the rows already in `stock_move_invoice_line_rel` stay wrong without it. Then it recomputes `account.move.picking_ids` for every invoice and credit note it touched, because that field is stored and it is what the *Delivery* and *Invoices* buttons show. Plain parametrized SQL plus that recompute, no extra dependency, and it does nothing on a database that has no such rows.

It leaves alone the links that `stock_picking_invoice_link` copies on purpose when a delivered invoice is reversed without a return: there the move stays linked to the reversed invoice too, while the bug replaced the links.

Tested on a 20.0 database with two orders (`invoice_policy = order`): A, the bug state (posted invoice, credit note, validated delivery linked only to the credit note); B, a delivered invoice reversed without a return.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| A, invoice `picking_ids` | none | the delivery |
| A, credit note `picking_ids` | the delivery | none |
| B, invoice and credit note `picking_ids` | the delivery | the delivery (unchanged) |

Log: `1 wrong links removed from credit notes, 1 links written to the invoice, 0 moves left with no invoice line of their own, 2 invoices and credit notes recomputed`. A second run finds nothing.

### Depends on

#2493 (`stock_picking_invoice_link`), already merged in 20.0.

### Tests

`0 failed, 0 error(s) of 10 tests` on a 20.0 database with #2493 installed.

items.title: [FIX] sale_stock_picking_invoice_link: link deliveries to the invoice, not the refund
items.body:
A move was treated as a refund whenever `to_refund` was set, and since 19.0 `stock_account` sets that field by `default=True` on every move. So an outgoing move of an order that has a credit note gets linked to the credit note instead of the invoice: the invoice ends up with no pickings and the credit note carries them.

The fix uses the same condition as the core (`sale_stock/models/stock.py`, `_action_synch_order`): a move refunds only when it comes back from the customer.

Writing the link also needs read access on `account.move.line`. `Many2many.write_real` reads the previous value before writing, and since 19.0 that read goes through `_search` with access checks (in 18.0 it only applied record rules). A user with Inventory access only, validating a delivery of an order with a credit note, got:

```
AccessError: Failed to read field stock.move.invoice_line_ids
You are not allowed to access 'Journal Item' (account.move.line) records.
```

The search was already done with `sudo()`; the write is too now.

Note the two fixes belong together: with the condition fixed and the write still unprivileged, the link would be written on *every* invoiced delivery, so the `AccessError` would stop being occasional and hit every warehouse user.

### Tests

The migration to 19.0 had hidden both problems by forcing `to_refund = False` on the delivered moves in two tests. Those lines are removed, so `test_link_transfer_after_invoice_creation` covers the condition again, and a new test validates a delivery of a refunded order as a user with `stock.group_stock_user` only.

Without the fix: `1 failed, 1 error(s) of 8 tests`. With it: `0 failed, 0 error(s) of 8 tests`.

items.title: [18.0][FIX] sale/purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link: link transit & subcontracting moves
items.body:
## Summary

Closes #2314.

`sale_stock_picking_invoice_link` and `purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link` only linked stock moves to invoice lines when the move's endpoint had usage `customer` / `supplier`. This excluded two real-world flows:

1. **Intercompany sale/purchase** — moves route through a `transit` location, so the picking ↔ invoice link was lost.
2. **Subcontracting (purchase only)** — receipts come from a subcontract location whose usage is `internal` but is flagged via `is_subcontracting_location` (provided by `mrp_subcontracting`).

### Changes

- Extracted the move-eligibility check into a predicate on `stock.move`:
  - `_is_purchase_invoice_link_candidate` — accepts `supplier`, `transit`, and any location with `is_subcontracting_location=True`.
  - `_is_sale_invoice_link_candidate` — accepts `customer` and `transit`.
- Both `*.order.line.get_stock_moves_link_invoice` and `stock.move.get_moves_link_invoice` now delegate to the predicate, so behaviour is consistent across the order-line and `stock.move.write` invoice-link paths.
- Subcontracting check uses `getattr(..., "is_subcontracting_location", False)` — no new dependency on `mrp_subcontracting`.
- Sale-side subcontracting is intentionally **not** addressed: the canonical flow is unclear and the issue itself flagged it as uncertain. Easy to follow up if a real case surfaces.

### Behaviour change to flag

Adding `transit` to the accepted usages is broader than just intercompany — any custom routing through a transit location will now produce picking ↔ invoice links. This is almost certainly the intended behaviour (the goods *are* moving as part of this SO/PO), but reviewers may want to sanity-check it.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test: `sale_stock_picking_invoice_link` → `test_intercompany_transit_link` — SO whose delivery move ends in a transit location → invoice line gets `move_line_ids`.
- [x] Unit test: `purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link` → `test_intercompany_transit_link` — PO whose receipt move starts from transit → bill line gets `move_line_ids`.
- [x] Unit test: `purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link` → `test_subcontracting_receipt_link` — PO whose receipt move starts from a subcontract location → bill line gets `move_line_ids`. Auto-skips when `mrp_subcontracting` is not installed.
- [x] All pre-existing tests in both modules still pass (no behaviour change for `customer`/`supplier` flows).
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` (pinned v0.6.8) — clean.
- [x] `flake8 --max-line-length=88` on changed files — clean.

## Module maturity

Beta (matches existing `development_status` of both modules).

items.title: [20.0][MIG] stock_picking_invoice_link: Migration to 20.0
items.body:
Standard migration + some improvements:
- `stock.move.product_uom` is now `uom_id` (tests)
- `stock.return.picking` wizard is gone, tests use `stock.picking._create_return()`
- Drop redundant `string` on `invoice_line_ids`
- Button icons moved to Material Symbols (`edit_square`, `local_shipping`)

PD: `stock_account` 20.0 defines `stock.move.invoice_line_ids` as a One2many over `account.move.line.stock_move_id`, and repair uses it. This module keeps it as the Many2many it always was (`stock_move_invoice_line_rel`), so invoice lines created or written with `stock_move_id` are also added to `move_line_ids`. That way repair keeps working. Tests added.

CC @ForgeFlow

items.title: [NEW][REF][16.0] stock_picking_invoice_link split to sale_stock_picking_invoice_link
items.body:
## Current Scenario

The stock_picking_invoice_link module, which adds the relationship between the invoice and stock picking, depends on the sale_stock module, but the purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link module depends on stock_picking_invoice_link, making it mandatory to install both the purchase and sale modules, thus losing modularity.

## Proposed Solution

The sale dependency on stock_picking_invoice_link was removed, and a new sale_stock_picking_invoice_link module was created. In this way, the stock_picking_invoice_link module is a base module for the sale_stock_picking_invoice_link and purchase_stock_picking_invoice_link modules, preserving modularity.

items.body:
Follow up to https://github.com/OCA/stock-logistics-workflow/pull/1388

New compute stored fields on large tables like this can lead to high
initialation times when we rely on the ORM.

Also, a new stored computed field was introduced in v15 along the former
computed method. We need to pre-compute it to avoid large migration
times.
